title: Savitri
hook: a childless king keeps offering with one verse, and the daughter he is given carries its name

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gandhari by the Ganga: she asked only to see her sons, and for one night the dead rose without anger.

A verse with a second name. Earlier this year, the verse to the sun that people call the Gayatri turned up in the older law books as the Savitri, the verse to the god Savitr. Keep that name in your pocket. In the Mahabharata, a sage sitting with the exiled Pandavas in the forest tells of a king with no child, and the verse he keeps offering with is that one. Last year we heard Savitri's whole story. This time we stay with the woman herself, starting where she starts: with her name.
screen: `THE GAYATRI HAS A SECOND NAME.` → `A KING WITH NO CHILD.` → `WHERE HER NAME CAME FROM.`

segments.voice: The king is Ashvapati, ruler of the Madras. The epic calls him good, truthful and generous, and grieved by one thing: there is no child in his house. So he takes up a discipline. He eats sparingly and keeps his senses in check. Again and again, into the sacred fire, he makes offerings with the Savitri verse, and he keeps it up a long time. Then one day the fire answers. The goddess Savitri herself rises out of it, pleased with him, and offers him a gift. He asks for children. She tells him a daughter will be born to him, full of radiance. When the girl comes, the king names her after the goddess who gave her: Savitri. A name that belonged to a verse, then to a goddess, now belongs to a baby. Think about what the verse asks for. In paraphrase: may the sun god stir our thoughts. And the girl named for it grows into a woman who keeps her thinking clear under pressure. She goes out and chooses. She hears a terrible warning and doesn't flinch. She will stand in front of Death and keep talking. The epic doesn't spell out that link. It gives her the name and lets her grow into it. One more turn. The law books hang this verse on the edges of the day, dawn and dusk, said while the light is changing. Savitri's whole story happens at an edge like that, between a life and its end: a verse for the turning of the light, made into a woman who stands in the turning and keeps her head.
screen: `ASHVAPATI OFFERS WITH THE VERSE` · `THE GODDESS RISES FROM THE FIRE` · `THE DAUGHTER IS NAMED SAVITRI` · `A NAME TO GROW INTO`

segments.voice: Bring to mind your own name, said out loud by someone who loves you, and ask gently who chose it and what they were hoping for; you don't need answers. Then let the name go and come back to the breath. If you know the Gayatri and you pray, you can say it once, silently.
Savitri. A princess named for the goddess who rose from the fire, and for the verse her father offered with.
Your line: Savitri. Her name was a verse before it was hers. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus who keep the daily twilight rite, sandhya, recite the Gayatri, also called the Savitri, at dawn and dusk; Savitri's story itself is retold at home and in temple talks.
